artifacts.summary: Confirms the three named defects (dead resolver key, no rc channel, dead verification call site) and discovers a fourth, load-bearing one: hook_path is built against a deployed extensions/<name>/scripts/ layout that never exists on disk, since provides.scripts always flattens into .claude/scripts/ -- fixing the resolver alone would still leave the nix preflight hook dark.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system's extension deploy pipeline, manifest.json's top-level `hooks` object (lifecycle hooks: preflight/context_injection/verification/postflight) is easy to author with a `scripts/<name>.sh` path that mirrors the SOURCE store layout, but the deploy pipeline always flattens `provides.scripts` entries into a flat `.claude/scripts/` directory -- `.claude/extensions/<name>/` only ever contains manifest.json on disk, never a nested scripts/ subdir (confirmed: installed_dirs is [] for every loaded extension). A hook_path built as `${ext_dir}/${hook_script}` will silently never resolve (masked by a silent -x no-op), even once the task_type->extension resolver itself is fixed. Any future hook path must resolve via basename against `.claude/scripts/`, not against the extension directory.

check-extension-docs.sh and script-inventory.sh validate manifest.json's provides.scripts and provides.hooks (the Claude-Code-native settings-hook file-copy array) against deployed reality, but never validate the top-level lifecycle `hooks` object's script paths -- a blind spot that let two extensions (nix, nvim) ship a hooks object pointing at a path that was never deployed, undetected by any existing lint.
